title: State machines for bounded agents
outcome: Explain state machines for bounded agents using the deciding step in this fictional service.
scenario: A parcel lookup state machine. An agent may follow idle→querying→checking→complete; complete is terminal.
given: A follows all four states. B follows idle→querying→complete. No other transitions are declared.

steps.label: Read arrows
steps.detail: The graph permits three forward transitions.

steps.label: Follow A
steps.detail: All adjacent pairs match permitted arrows.

steps.label: Inspect B
steps.detail: Querying→complete skips checking and is invalid.

explanation: A state machine bounds action order. A plausible final state does not establish that the path was valid.

counterfactual.change: Add checking→querying as a permitted retry.
counterfactual.prediction: That retry becomes valid; querying→complete stays forbidden.
counterfactual.reason: Adding one arrow does not authorise unrelated shortcuts.

student_task: Trace A and B through the state diagram. Name B’s forbidden transition and explain whether adding checking→querying permits that shortcut.
teacher_answer: The graph permits three forward transitions. All adjacent pairs match permitted arrows. Querying→complete skips checking and is invalid. Changed case: That retry becomes valid; querying→complete stays forbidden. Adding one arrow does not authorise unrelated shortcuts.
project_evidence: For the Grounded Learning Service, retain an annotated trace and the changed-case result. Name the contract or evidence that makes the deciding step valid, so another team can review it.
limits: This graph checks sequence, not the correctness of the fetched parcel data.
review_note: Individually authored fictional practice, distinct from the reserved independent case. These stipulated records illustrate reasoning; no real service execution or learner outcome is claimed.
